## Overview

LRPDID105 is the **dispersion-prior sensitivity companion** to [LRPDID10](../lrp-rli-did-010/), and the low-denominator half of a two-fit check whose other half is [LRPDID106](../lrp-rli-did-106/). Same model, same data, same sampler settings; only the shape of the dispersion prior differs.

| | LRPDID10 (reference) | LRPDID105 (this model) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| dispersion prior | $\kappa \sim \text{HalfNormal}(50)$ | $1/\sqrt{\kappa} \sim \text{HalfNormal}(0.25)$ |
| near-Binomial limit $\kappa \gg n$ | effectively unreachable | reachable |
| test length $n$ | 18 | 18 |
| everything else | — | identical |

## Why this model exists

A half-normal prior placed on the Beta-Binomial **concentration** cannot reach the near-Binomial limit $\kappa \gg n$, so for a long test it imposes a *floor* on the estimated over-dispersion rather than letting the data set it. At $n = 170$ the family default's prior median already implies roughly 5.9 times Binomial variance, and coming within 10 % of Binomial variance would need $\kappa$ beyond anything the prior gives real mass to. At 18 items the same prior is far more permissive, because a modest $\kappa$ is already large relative to $n$.

Reparameterising onto the **dispersion scale** $u = 1/\sqrt{\kappa}$ — the form the ITT and level-factor families adopted for the same reason — puts real prior mass at $u \to 0$, so the model is free to conclude there is no extra variation beyond Binomial. $\kappa$ is retained as a deterministic transform, so every downstream table reads the same way.

## How to read the pair

Read LRPDID105 and LRPDID106 together; neither is informative alone.

- **Both stable.** The concentration prior is a nuisance choice the arm gaps do not turn on, and the family default needs no change.
- **The 170-item fit moves, the 18-item fit does not.** The prior's ceiling — not the data — was setting the dispersion at high denominators. That is a reason to revisit the family *default*, not to reinterpret one outcome.
- **Both move.** The dispersion prior is doing more work than intended across the family.

_Sign convention and reading rules as LRPDID10._ The dispersion prior changes no term's causal status: $\tau_{t2}$ remains the randomised t2 assignment contrast and the t3 quantities remain randomised treatment-schedule contrasts rather than treated-versus-untreated effects.
